title: Issak
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In 1620, as the Thirty Years' War spreads across Europe, a lone Japanese marksman called Issak fights as a mercenary while hunting the man who murdered his master and fled Japan (Kodansha blurb via AniList). His quarry, Lorenzo (Renzo), carries a twin matchlock made by the same master and relishes war (Gizmodo). Catholic and Protestant forces, royals and witch hunts form the backdrop (Gizmodo; MU Politics Involving Religion). Complete in 19 volumes.
life_message: Loyalty to one's master and skill carried with discipline give a man purpose amid a chaotic war, though revenge and war are morally murky.

folkways.japan: Issak's devotion to his master reflects Japanese samurai ideals of loyalty to one's teacher, set against European feudal politics.

delivery.evidence: Gizmodo describes morally murky war and 'philosophical quandaries' carried by action, not speeches.
delivery.note: The contrast between Issak's purpose and Renzo's love of battle carries the themes (to verify depth).

winners_losers: Sympathy lies with Issak's loyalty and skill; Lorenzo, who 'gets off on' war, is his foil. How Catholic and Protestant sides are treated is not established by the sources.
